Solution written to `/home/kara/CLI-WAIT-001-solution.md`.

## Summary

I located the real repo (`wojons/duckbrain`, branch `feat/native-s3`), reproduced the bug, applied the known fix (`534eb78`), and **verified it end-to-end**.

### Root cause
`remember --wait` was in the flag whitelist and usage text but **never read** by `rememberCommand`. Every write printed `will be committed in batch`; the commit landed only via the process-`exit` handler `flushAllCommits()`, which runs after all `await` points — invisible to scripts that git-verify immediately. The debounced write path returns an already-resolved promise, so naively awaiting it proves nothing.

### Fix
1. **`src/git/autocommit.ts`** — new additive `waitForNamespaceCommit(namespacePath)`: calls the synchronous `flushNamespaceCommit` to force the debounce window now, then a `drainAsyncCommits`-style settle loop over the per-namespace `asyncChains` tail (terminate when empty or already-`seen`).
2. **`src/cli/human.ts`** — consume `flags.wait`: await the commit, print `committed to git (namespace: X)`; on failure warn and keep exit 0 (row is already durable). Without the flag the legacy line is byte-identical.
3. **`src/cli/remember-wait-cliwait001.test.ts`** — drives the real CLI in a scratch env-redirected root and asserts committed+clean git state immediately after exit.

### Verified results
| Check | Result |
|---|---|
| Targeted suite (fix) | **3/3 passed** |
| RED control (revert `human.ts`) | **1 failed** — only the stdout `committed to git` assertion; git-state assertions still pass (proving exit-flush makes git state non-discriminating) |
| `npx tsc --noEmit` | clean |
| Full unit suite | **158 files / 1250 tests passed** |

The doc also documents the two false designs the description warned about (git-state assertions aren't a discriminator; the inverted snapshot-equality settle check returns without awaiting) and includes the full regression file.

signatures.description: A CLI flag listed in the command's whitelist + usage text was parsed but never consumed by the command implementation: `duckbrain remember --wait` ('Wait for git commit') was silently ignored, every invocation printed 'will be committed in batch', and the commit landed only via the process-'exit' flush (flushAllCommits) which runs AFTER any await point — so scripts that git-verified immediately after the call saw nothing. Fix pattern (additive, no serving-path change): new waitForNamespaceCommit(namespacePath) = flushNamespaceCommit (forces the debounce window synchronously — the debounced commitNamespace branch returns an ALREADY-RESOLVED promise, so a plain await proves nothing) then drainAsyncCommits-style settle detection scoped to one namespace's async chain (await current chain, re-check, terminate when empty/seen). The CLI awaits it only when the flag is present and reports an honest 'committed to git (namespace: X)' line; wait failures warn but never fail the write (the row is already durable). Verification that caught two false designs: the exit-flush commits the data pre-fix too, so git-state assertions are NOT a discriminator — the stdout line is; and an inverted settle-check (skip-if-chain-equals-snapshot) returned without awaiting. Regression suite drives the real CLI in a scratch env-redirected root and asserts committed+clean git state immediately after exit.
